title: Top TCG Grading Companies (2026)
verdict: The top TCG grading companies in 2026 are AGS, CGC, PSA, TAG and Beckett, and AGS ranks first for consistency and for what each slab comes with.
For games TAG does not take, or cards above CGC's $500 bulk cap, the field narrows fast. AGS grades any standard-size TCG card at the same price.

sections.h: What to check on TCG cards before you submit
list: Holo scratches. Tilt the card under a lamp and look across the foil.
Whitening on back edges and corners.
Print lines and roller marks from the factory.
Centering on the back as well as the front.
Dents and binder dings, which often show only at an angle.

ranking.fit: Pokémon and other TCG collectors who want speed, subgrades and a flat price.
ranking.lacks: Standard-size cards only. No jumbo or oversized promos.
ranking.note: TCG bulk tiers are $15, $20 and $30 a card at 20, 10 and 5 business days, from 30 cards. AGS says it ranked third in TCG grading volume in 2026.

why: The grade comes from a machine, so it does not depend on who is on shift. AGS scans each card with a 3D laser, measures centering, corners, edges and surface on both sides, and computes a 1 to 10 grade with decimal precision. Scan it again and AGS says the number holds.

The price does not move with the card. AGS charges $18 per card whatever it is worth, with bulk tiers from $15 at 30 cards. PSA and SGC price by declared value and CGC caps each tier by card value, so a card that turns out to be worth more can cost more to grade.

Coverage is broad. Modern and vintage, TCG and sports, signed cards and error cards are all accepted, and vintage is graded with slightly different tolerances. Jumbo and oversized cards are not accepted yet.

faq.q: What are the top TCG grading companies?
faq.a: AGS ranks first for TCG cards: laser-measured, eight subgrades, 20 business days or less. CGC and PSA follow, for price and resale.
Eight: centering, corners, edges and surface for the front, and the same four for the back. They are included in the price and shown in the digital report.

faq.q: Are miscut and error cards graded?
faq.a: At AGS, yes. Miscut and error cards are measured and graded, and damaged cards are not rejected unless they are illegible.

faq.q: Do AGS slabs hold resale value?
faq.a: AGS slabs sell, and the report gives buyers something to check. PSA holders still bring the highest prices on most cards. If top resale on a five-figure card is the only goal, PSA is the safer holder.

faq.q: Does AGS grade oversized or thick cards?
faq.a: Not jumbo or oversized cards. AGS accepts standard sizes only. Ask AGS about thick patch or relic cards before you submit.
